assessments.reasoning: OSI CMS record 484 matches the claimed digest and titles the article “Open Software License 2.1.” It prescribes “Licensed under the Open Software License version 2.1” immediately following the copyright notice and supplies the grant.
The pinned Index scope admits a separately identified historical license and requires member-level evidence for an edition. Record 484 supplies that evidence for 2.1.

Rosen’s archived request covers all OSL versions prior to 3.0, which includes 2.1. His later message distinguishes the ordinary and Non-Profit forms and records his continued support for the 3.0 versions.

challenge.method: Compared the supersession note’s link label and destination with the article’s own title, notice and section 10, then checked termination and approval inferences.
challenge.results: The label names ordinary OSL 3.0 but the href contains nposl-3-0. The body unambiguously identifies 2.1. No grant-specific termination follows, the SPDX deprecation flag is false, and OSI’s false CMS approval flag and SPDX’s true approval field cannot resolve board history.

limitations: The exact successor cannot be established from the note. Historical classification determines neither rights under a particular grant nor OSI board action, SPDX deprecation or installation eligibility.
reasoning: OSI record 484 documents the 2.1 license. Its superseded category, opening editorial note and Rosen’s pre-3.0 chronology support the proposed local historical classification even though the note’s successor link is ambiguous.
